title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
The Trump administration is shifting its stance on artificial intelligence. Following reports of hacking incidents at OpenAI, officials are considering new controls for the industry, marking a move away from the previous hands-off policy.

Meanwhile, Meta is deepening its AI integration by adding its Meta AI chatbot directly into Threads direct messages. In the retail sector, Chinese robotics firms are increasingly filling gaps in the UK market, stepping in to address labor shortages and weak productivity growth.

Big Tech is facing scrutiny over massive AI spending. Both Alphabet and Tesla saw stock impacts as investors worry that heavy investment is draining free cash flow. Markets are now watching closely to see if Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon face similar pressure.

In the financial sector, the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady between 3.5% and 3.75%. Chair Jerome Powell noted there is no quick fix for high prices. Investor skepticism remains, however. Jeffrey Gundlach pointed out that the bond market suggests investors are doubtful the Fed will act aggressively enough to curb inflation.

Legal and hardware news rounded out the week. Johnson & Johnson has proposed a settlement of up to $5.5 billion to resolve long-standing lawsuits alleging its talc products cause cancer. Separately, Apple has launched a new device leasing program with Klarna, even as the company navigates supply chain constraints caused by a global memory chip shortage.
